Synopsis:
    Ireland's Health Service Executive (HSE) was fined a record €645,000 by the Data Protection Commission for storing medical records in severely neglected conditions — including a turf shed, disused bathrooms, and derelict buildings — with some records destroyed by mould or contaminated by animal droppings. The DPC ordered a full audit, remediation of unfit storage facilities, and implementation of a proper records management system. The HSE accepted the findings and apologised.
